<explanation>
Below is a tailored guide for creating a complete, accurate system-design diagram of the git-filter-repo project.  Treat this as an instruction set for your diagram, not the diagram itself.

1. Identify Project Type and Purpose
   • Type: Open-source CLI tool + library.
   • Purpose: Rewriting Git repository history at scale via a Python-based library, driving Git’s fast-export/fast-import.

2. Key Architectural Components
   a. User & CLI Layer
      – git-filter-repo (single‐file Python script  
        • Entry point on $PATH  
        • Parses CLI flags, loads pyproject.toml metadata  
      – contrib/filter-repo-demos  
        • Example extensions & custom scripts demonstrating use of the library.  
   b. Core Library Layer
      – git_filter_repo.py  
        • Implements streaming pipeline:  
          1. Invocation of “git fast-export”  
          2. Parsing of commits, trees, blobs  
          3. Filter callbacks & transform logic  
          4. Pruning/renaming operations  
          5. Generation of new stream for “git fast-import”  
      – Plugin API  
        • User-provided Python callbacks (via filters, path selectors, mailmap handlers)  
   c. External Dependencies
      – Git (≥2.36.0)  
        • fast-export, fast-import, update-ref, gc  
      – Python 3.6+  
      – CI / Automation  
        • .github/workflows/test.yml: runs tests on each push/PR  
   d. Test & Validation Layer
      – t/ directory  
        • Shell scripts (t9390-t9394) and helper scripts for run_tests, run_coverage  
        • Test-library functions (test-lib.sh, test-lib-functions.sh)  
        • Test data subdirs for edge cases (empty commits, unusual filenames, mailmap, merges)  
   e. Documentation Layer
      – Documentation/  
        • Contributing.md, FAQ.md, examples, conversion cheat‐sheets  
      – README.md, INSTALL.md  

3. Relationships & Data Flows
   • User invokes git-filter-repo → CLI script  
     → Core library invokes Git fast-export (stream out old history)  
     → Streaming parser breaks input into objects  
     → Filter pipeline applies “keep vs remove”, “rename”, “prune empty/degenerate”  
     → Modified stream fed into Git fast-import → Writes rewritten history  
     → Post-import: update-ref, git gc  
   • CLI can load contrib/demo scripts → Extends core library at filter callbacks  
   • Tests exercise CLI + library → verify intended behavior on sample repos  
   • CI workflow → triggers tests on GitHub  

4. Architectural Patterns & Principles
   • Layered design: CLI → Library → External Git  
   • Streaming pipeline: handles arbitrarily large repos without full in-memory load  
   • Plugin/extensibility API: users supply Python callbacks rather than shell hacks  
   • Safety by design: fresh-clone enforcement, automatic pruning & repacking  
   • Single-file CLI distribution for ease of install  

5. Diagramming Guidelines for an Open-Source Tool
   • Emphasize Core vs Extension points  
     – Show core library box with “Filter Pipeline” inside  
     – Show plugin hooks where contrib demos or user scripts attach  
   • Show integration with external system (Git) as a distinct service/component  
   • Include test harness as a parallel consumer of CLI & library  
   • Show CI as an outer orchestration component  

6. Visual Elements to Include
   – Clear labels on each box (e.g., “git-filter-repo CLI”, “Core Library (git_filter_repo.py)”, “Git fast-export/import”)  
   – Directional arrows for data flow (old history → filtering → new history)  
   – Color‐coding or distinct shapes  
     • Blue: internal components (CLI, library)  
     • Green: external systems (Git commands, filesystem)  
     • Orange: extension points (contrib demos, user scripts)  
     • Gray: CI & documentation artifacts  
   – Annotation of key protocols (e.g., “stdin/stdout stream”), file formats, version requirements  

7. Detail Checklist
   – Show How CLI flags map into library options  
   – Show pruning & renaming sub-components within filter pipeline  
   – Depict post-processing steps: update-ref, gc  
   – Illustrate test directories invoking CLI with sample repos  
   – Indicate installation path (pyproject.toml, Makefile, single‐file distribution)  

By following these guidelines you’ll produce a diagram that:
 – Captures all critical layers (User/CLI, Core Library, Git, Tests, CI, Docs)  
 – Shows precise data flows and extension points  
 – Reflects the project’s streaming, plugin-based architecture  
 – Uses clear labels, arrows, and color‐coding to differentiate component types  
</explanation>
